system.name: bpftime
system.one_liner: a userspace runtime that extends applications with eBPF-compatible extensions, safely and efficiently, without kernel involvement

components.name: eBPF Program Source Code
components.role: source code input to the standard eBPF toolchain (reused from eBPF)

components.name: eBPF compiler
components.role: compiles eBPF program source into bytecode (reused from eBPF)

components.name: eBPF application
components.role: the resulting user application containing bytecode and the loader library

components.name: eBPF bytecode
components.role: compiled eBPF bytecode inside the eBPF application

components.name: libbpf
components.role: the standard eBPF userspace library used to load bytecode

components.name: UbiBPF Loader
components.role: loads and prepares an eBPF application for execution atop bpftime's userspace runtime

components.name: Binary Rewriter
components.role: rewrites the target binary to redirect eBPF hook points to bpftime

components.name: JIT compiler
components.role: JIT-compiles eBPF bytecode; reused eBPF component, appears in both the UbiBPF Loader and the kernel-side chain

components.name: verifier
components.role: verifies eBPF bytecode safety; reused eBPF component, appears in both the UbiBPF Loader and the kernel-side chain

components.name: Syscall Interposition
components.role: interposes on eBPF-related system calls, the narrow waist where bpftime intercepts the existing eBPF ecosystem

components.name: UbiBPF user runtime
components.role: bpftime's userspace runtime executing loaded eBPF extensions in-process

components.name: Target process
components.role: the host application(s) being extended, containing uprobe/tracepoint/syscall hook points

components.name: uprobe
components.role: a userspace probe hook point in the target process (reused from eBPF)

components.name: userspace tracepoint
components.role: a new userspace tracepoint hook point introduced by bpftime

components.name: Syscall tracepoint
components.role: a new syscall-tracepoint hook point introduced by bpftime for attaching extensions to syscalls in userspace

components.name: UbiBPF maps
components.role: shared map mechanism for sharing data across extensions, bridging kernel and userspace

components.name: syscall
components.role: represents syscall events flowing between UbiBPF maps and the kernel-side hook points

components.name: eBPF runtime
components.role: the traditional in-kernel eBPF runtime executing kernel-side eBPF programs (reused from eBPF)

components.name: tracepoint
components.role: a kernel tracepoint hook point (reused from eBPF)

components.name: kprobe
components.role: a kernel kprobe hook point (reused from eBPF)

components.name: socket
components.role: a kernel socket hook point (reused from eBPF)

content.key_idea: bpftime reimplements the eBPF toolchain's narrow waist (syscall interposition and shared maps) in userspace, letting existing eBPF bytecode load and JIT-compile into a UbiBPF user runtime that attaches to uprobes and new userspace tracepoints without kernel involvement.
content.reading_order: Left to right: the standard eBPF toolchain (source, compiler, bytecode/libbpf) feeds bpftime's UbiBPF Loader; top (Userspace) and bottom (Kernel) halves mirror load-verify-JIT-execute chains reaching each side's hook points.

palette.used_for: white fill for components reused from standard eBPF (e.g., verifier, JIT compiler, eBPF runtime, uprobe, tracepoint, kprobe, socket)
orange fill for components new to bpftime (e.g., UbiBPF Loader, Binary Rewriter, Syscall Interposition, UbiBPF user runtime, UbiBPF maps, userspace/syscall tracepoint)
blue arrows showing the compile-and-load execution flow
green arrows showing the flow when an eBPF extension executes

encoding.color_means: white marks components reused unchanged from standard eBPF; orange marks components bpftime adds or modifies; blue arrows trace the one-time compile-and-load path; green arrows trace the repeated runtime path when an extension executes
encoding.line_style_means: plain colored arrows carry directional execution flow (blue, green); black double-headed arrows (white fill, black outline) mark bidirectional shared-memory access to UbiBPF maps, distinct from the directional flows
encoding.emphasis: Consistently coloring every bpftime-original component orange against an all-white standard-eBPF backdrop lets the reader see, at a glance, exactly how much of the existing eBPF toolchain bpftime reuses versus replaces
reusable_patterns: two-color component coding (new vs. reused/existing) applied consistently across an entire architecture diagram
two differently-colored arrow types distinguishing a one-time setup flow from a repeated runtime flow
mirrored top/bottom sub-pipelines for two execution environments (userspace vs. kernel) of the same underlying technology

evidence: bpftime identifies a narrow waist in the current eBPF ecosystem and interposes at this point.
We implemented bpftime in 13,000 lines of code; Figure 4 provides the high-level design.
White components are from eBPF; orange components are new to bpftime.

summary: Figure 4 shows bpftime's design, color-coding every box white (reused from eBPF) or orange (new to bpftime). On the left, a standard eBPF toolchain compiles source into bytecode loaded via libbpf. This feeds bpftime's UbiBPF Loader, whose Binary Rewriter, JIT compiler, verifier, and Syscall Interposition chain (blue, load-time arrows) prepare an eBPF application for bpftime's UbiBPF user runtime, which attaches to a Target process's uprobe and two new hook points, userspace tracepoint and Syscall tracepoint. A mirrored, unmodified kernel-side chain (verifier, JIT compiler, eBPF runtime) still serves kernel tracepoint, kprobe, and socket hooks. Both halves share data through UbiBPF maps, accessed bidirectionally (black double arrows) and along green arrows that trace an extension's actual execution. The whole system spans a dashed Userspace/Kernel boundary, showing bpftime's user-level reimplementation running alongside the original in-kernel path.
summary_zh: 图4展示bpftime设计:白色为沿用eBPF组件,橙色为新增组件。左侧工具链经libbpf进入UbiBPF Loader,供运行时挂载uprobe与新tracepoint;内核侧保留verifier/JIT路径,双方经maps共享数据。
notes: layout-proposal: mirrored-userspace-kernel-pipeline — a Userspace/Kernel layered split where each half runs a near-mirrored load/verify/JIT/execute sub-pipeline, fed by a separate linear eBPF-toolchain flow on the left; the source caption is truncated before explaining the fourth (white/black-outline) arrow style, so that arrow's exact meaning is inferred from the image alone.
